items.headline: Qatar’s mediators return to Tehran as Iran hardens its terms
items.summary: the delegation arrived Friday for a fresh round on an interim deal, while four tankers burned after hitting mines in the strait and the Revolutionary Guards halted two more ships.
items.matters: every week without a memorandum keeps a fifth of global oil supply on a war footing.
items.body: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday as part of efforts to reach a deal between the US and Iran, an official briefed on the talks told Reuters. Qatar presented a draft peace plan to Iran on Sunday, according to an official briefed on negotiations. But a senior Iranian official dismissed the proposals as unacceptable and said Tehran would maintain its nuclear position. Washington wants nuclear issues included from the start of negotiations. Tehran demands that the US first end its port blockade and lift oil export sanctions. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Wednesday that Tehran remained in close contact with intermediaries to review ideas that could ensure the implementation of its own seven-day proposal aimed at ending the war in the Middle East. On Thursday, President Donald Trump said Vice President JD Vance's outreach to Iran concerned medical supplies, following US media reports linking it to efforts to revive peace talks. Meanwhile, four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said Thursday, a day after the US military said it cleared key routes through the waterway. "Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement. Meanwhile, Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Friday said two oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified "incidents" while attempting to transit what Tehran considers an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz. "Two offending oil tankers, one in the eastern part and the other in the western part of the Strait of Hormuz, which were attempting to pass through the unauthorised route, encountered incidents and were brought to a halt in the waters south of the strait," the IRGC said in a statement. items.headline: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 European flights in a second wave
items.summary: Finnair, Ryanair, Aer Lingus, Wizz Air, LOT and SAS flights made unplanned landings or were escorted by fighter jets, with nothing found on board.
items.matters: cheap, deniable disruption is now a weekly cost on European aviation, and nobody has claimed it.
items.body: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 affected flights around Europe from Ireland to Bulgaria, the second wave this week, forcing some to make unplanned landings and prompting fighter jets to escort or intercept others. While no country has attributed blame for the threats, they come as many European officials are accusing Russia of masterminding sabotage and "hybrid attacks" - often cheap, easily deniable and not expected to trigger an armed response. Denmark, Poland and Romania, all affected by Thursday's disruptions, have previously accused Moscow directly, while Germany blamed Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport in August. Britain has blamed Russia in the past but linked Iran to a suspected plot to attack a US air base. Both Russia and Iran deny any involvement. Eric Schouten, head of the aviation security group Dyami, said most of the countries affected supported Ukraine in its war against Russia's invasion. "From a geopolitical view, I'm thinking, you always have to think about the scenario of hybrid warfare, where a country in this way - today we are looking at Russia, right? - is attacking us on multiple fronts, from railways to supermarkets to blood banks, most recently. The energy sector, the internet sector, and the aviation sector are among those," he said. Over France, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office said he had sent fighter jets to intercept an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome and escort it to an air force base at Evreux after the pilot did not cooperate with authorities as expected. No reason was given for the pilot's behaviour. Bulgaria's air force said its fighter jets had escorted three airliners to the ground. Ryanair planes from Copenhagen and Madrid to Sofia landed as planned while a flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Plovdiv, Bulgaria's second city. Spanish authorities received three emailed bomb threats in under 20 minutes involving two Air Europa departures from Madrid to Paris and four inbound Iberia flights from Rome and Milan, Spain's Guardia Civil said. Several aircraft in Madrid were halted or returned to their stands and passengers were disembarked while planes were inspected. In Warsaw, a LOT flight to Paris was stopped as it taxied towards take-off and passengers were transferred to another aircraft. A flight from Cork in Ireland was delayed 90 minutes after the airport received a threat, the airport operator said. Italian media reported that a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw had been diverted to Vienna. Two Easyjet flights from Britain, one flight from Ireland and one from Greece landed as…

items.body: Israel's President Isaac Herzog is poised to give Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to lead coalition talks. Neither Mr Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc nor the opposition secured enough seats for a parliamentary majority in last week's election. Mr Eisenkot faces an uphill struggle amid a divided political landscape, and Israel could be facing weeks of delays. Link copied Share Share article Israel's President Isaac Herzog will wait until Sunday to announce whether he will tap Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival to begin the process of forming a new coalition government, amid ongoing accusations from the prime minister and other right-wing politicians the election was "stolen." Last week's ballot delivered an unsurprisingly inconclusive result, with neither Mr Netanyahu and his ruling right-wing coalition nor the band of challengers led by former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot receiving enough support to govern in majority. Coalition governments are the norm in Israel, and after being presented with the official results of the election, Mr Herzog has had the task of meeting representatives from each party to seek advice on who they believe is best placed to begin negotiations. While the meetings were underway on Thursday night, local time, two competing groups of protesters gathered outside the president's residence in central Jerusalem. One group called for a "unity government" comprising Mr Netanyahu and Mr Eisenkot's parties, and a larger group demanded a Jewish-Arab coalition to stabilise the country. Mr Eisenkot's own Yashar party, along with fellow "change" camp parties Together, Yisrael Beiteinu and the Democrats, all recommended the former general be given the first shot at forming government. Mr Netanyahu's Likud, the far-right Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism parties led by internationally sanctioned ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, and the ultra-Orthodox Shas all backed the incumbent to begin the negotiations. It defended the approach by arguing there had been "wild incitement and fierce persecution" of their community during the debate over whether Haredi men should be forced to complete compulsory military service. The two Arab-Israeli or Palestinian-Israeli parties, the Joint List and the United Arab List, also recommended Mr Eisenkot. items.headline: Nasdaq confirms a correction, down 5.52% to 24,315.00
items.summary: the S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73 and the Dow 3.44% to 51,523.06, wiping roughly $3tn of S&P market value in a session.

items.body: THE Nasdaq Composite ended sharply lower on Thursday (Nov 5), notching its deepest one-day drop in 19 months and confirming it was in a correction, as chipmakers sank on fears of tougher AI regulation after Democrats won control of the US Congress . Democratic wins on Tuesday, including in states where opposition to new data centres has mounted, fuelled concerns that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout that has helped lift stocks to record highs this year. “Investors appear to be recognising that some newly elected members of Congress and governors are looking to slow the pace of AI infrastructure development,” said Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp. The Nasdaq Composite logged its biggest daily drop since President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariff announcement in April 2025. The index ended down more than 10 per cent from its Oct 6 record-high close, confirming a technical correction. While chipmakers that provide components for AI data centres were among the deepest decliners, other large-cap tech stocks also lost ground after rallying on Wednesday. Meta Platforms, Amazon.com and Alphabet fell. Data centre operators IREN and Applied Digital, neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius Group all tumbled. AI-exposed utilities and equipment suppliers GE Vernova and Constellation Energy also dropped. Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX both dropped. Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars backing Republican candidates in the midterm elections. Qualcomm fell after the chipmaker fell short of Wall Street estimates for fourth-quarter smartphone chip sales. The Nasdaq declined 5.52 per cent to 24,315.00 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 3.44 per cent to 51,523.06 points. Following Thursday’s selloff, the S&P 500 remains up 7.4 per cent in 2026, while the Nasdaq is up 4.6 per cent. Volume on US exchanges was very heavy, with 26.9 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.7 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions. On Wednesday, the S&P 500 clocked its biggest one-day percentage gain in three months, as political uncertainty eased, boosting risk appetite. Some analysts said a divided government in Washington could lead to fewer sharp legislative changes and may make it harder to agree on fiscal spending. Chipmakers were by far the worst hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sliding 12.25% for the day. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA), which recently relinquished its title as the world's most valuable listed company, slumped nearly 10% on Thursday, while rival AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) slid 17%. Losses spilled over into Friday's Asian session, with South Korea's KOSPI on the verge of a 20% wipeout from late-October levels, while Japan's Nikkei 225 entered a bear market. The Democratic Party's sweep of the midterm elections– where it secured majorities in both chambers of Congress– sparked heightened concerns over more regulatory scrutiny towards AI development and data center construction. Texas Governor-Elect, Democrat Gina Hinojosa, called for a pause on any new data center construction until there were laws to protect citizens in place. Her comments reflected a broader rhetoric among Democratic lawmakers, especially amid growing voter pushback against more data center construction across the country. items.body: Tech & Startup Desk Photo: Reuters/ Carlos Barria Anthropic is considering releasing a new AI model to counter momentum gained by OpenAI since the launch of GPT-6 Astra, according to three sources cited in a Reuters report. The deliberations come as the company prepares for an expected public listing, and shortly after chief executive Dario Amodei publicly urged the industry to slow down. Amodei's essay on September 12 called for a deceleration in model development and warned of swarms of AI agents outpacing human control. The piece drew support from OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk. According to the sources, the timing of a potential Anthropic release is being weighed against competitive pressure from a direct rival. OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra on September 3, highlighting advances in computer use, software engineering, cybersecurity, and professional work. The model has drawn a strong response from business users and developers, prompting some investors to reassess Anthropic's standing as the leading supplier of enterprise AI tools. Data from corporate expense platform Ramp shows Astra accounting for roughly 13% of enterprise AI spending, compared with about 8% for Anthropic's Claude Fable. On OpenRouter, a platform that routes developer traffic across models, users spent more on OpenAI models than on Anthropic's last week, the first time OpenAI has led on that measure in more than two and a half years, Reuters reports. Anthropic is assessing the safety of its next model as part of its release considerations, one person familiar with the matter said to Reuters. Some discussions have centred on how to balance investment in new releases with efforts to improve profitability, as rising interest rates push investors to focus on when returns will arrive. Anthropic declined to comment to Reuters on the matter. Some existing and prospective investors said they do not view Astra as a serious threat, pointing to Anthropic's lead in enterprise AI and the time it takes to displace established vendors at large companies. Anthropic's annualised revenue run rate exceeded $65 billion by the end of July, up from about $9 billion at the end of 2025, and it projects 2028 revenue of roughly $190 billion to $200 billion, Reuters has previously reported. OpenAI's run rate passed $40 billion in July. Investors expect leadership among Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and other major developers to change hands repeatedly as new model generations arrive. A larger concern, some said, as per the report, is the rise of open-source and open-weight…

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic both claim to have dented the Exponential Time Hypothesis
items.summary: each published AI-generated arguments against the 27-year-old conjecture, formalised in Lean, that underpins much of complexity theory.
items.matters: if it verifies, a machine found a result humans assumed was out of reach, and peer review gets an urgent new problem.
items.body: Tech & Startup Desk OpenAI and Anthropic have separately announced AI-generated mathematical results that they say overturn a longstanding assumption in theoretical computer science, potentially reshaping researchers' understanding of computational complexity. The claims concern the Exponential Time Hypothesis, or ETH, a conjecture developed in the late 1990s that has influenced computer science research for more than two decades. The hypothesis concerns the difficulty of solving certain computational problems, particularly those involving Boolean satisfiability, where a computer must determine whether a collection of logical conditions can be satisfied simultaneously. Researchers have long believed that solving these problems inevitably requires computational effort that grows exponentially with the size of the problem. OpenAI said its internal AI system generated a purported refutation on October 16, which was subsequently formalised using Lean, a mathematical proof verification system. Anthropic also published an AI-generated research paper presenting a subexponential-time algorithm for a related satisfiability problem, accompanied by formal verification materials. If validated, the findings could force researchers to reconsider hundreds of theoretical results that rely on…

items.body: Blender end of life (EOL) and end of support (EOS) dates: 16 Blender versions have reached EOL, including Blender 5.1 (EOL date: Jul 14, 2026 ) — no longer receiving security updates or patches. Blender 5.2.3 LTS is the current supported release, with support through Jul 14, 2028 — 2 versions in active support. Also see Docker Engine end of life dates for related end-of-life information. Your Blender end of life date decides how long a project can stay on one build before bugs go unfixed. Blender is a free and open source 3D creation suite, and its latest version , Blender 5.2, is a long-term support build backed through July 2028, so most studios only need to know which line they run. Blender is open-source software for 3D modelling, modeling tools, sculpting, rigging, texturing, UV mapping, simulation, compositing, motion tracking, video editing, visual effects, motion graphics, virtual reality, video games, rendering and animation. Every build among all Blender releases has a published support window, and the table below shows where each recent one stands as of October 2026. This version history shows the pattern: a stable release arrives roughly every four months, and only the LTS builds live longer than a single cycle. Anything below the 4.5 line is already unsupported, and the current stable release is 5.2. Earlier Blender releases and their previous versions remain online, but only for reference. The Blender LTS program exists so long-lasting projects can stay on one stable build with 2 years of fixes, and every LTS build gets the full 2 years. An LTS build gets no new features and no API changes. Each LTS release starts at the same support level as other builds, then drops to critical bugfixes once its successor ships. Non-LTS builds are covered only until the next release, so their window is short. Two LTS builds are maintained today. Blender 5.2 LTS launched on 14 July 2026, and Blender 4.5 LTS is supported until July 2027. Both follow the same lifecycle, so you can plan around either one. The 4.2 build, with a release date of 16 July 2024, finished its two years in July 2026, while 3.6 closed in June 2025. Older builds such as 3.3, 2.93 and 2.83 stay available to download, but they get nothing further. For the two years of an LTS window, critical bug fixes from the newest build are ported back. Canonical also sells enterprise support for LTS builds on Ubuntu, and that service covers the same window. Once the two years end, the fixes stop and the build is retired. items.body: FINAL FANTASY XIV groups its servers, called Worlds, into data centres in four regions: Japan, North America, Europe and Oceania. This page explains how Worlds and data centres fit together, how World Visit and Data Center Travel let you play elsewhere, what congested and preferred Worlds mean, how to change your Home World, and who can play together, mostly from Square Enix’s own posts about its data centres. Checked against Patch 7.57 (13 October 2026) and Square Enix’s Lodestone post of 2 November 2026 on Patch 7.58. We’ll update this page when Patch 7.58 is out on Tuesday 10 November 2026, after a maintenance Square Enix expects to last 24 hours. Data centre and World names below are a snapshot of what Square Enix’s posts name, not a live server list. Each region has a physical data centre (the hardware), split into logical data centres , each a group of Worlds. Your character is made on one World, its Home World. The data centres Square Enix’s posts name: Japan’s other logical data centres are not named in Square Enix’s Steam posts. New Worlds come in with expansions of a data centre: Square Enix added two Worlds each to Chaos (Sagittarius, Phantom) and Light (Alpha, Raiden) in Patch 6.18 ( Square Enix on Steam , 23 June 2022), and a new North American data centre with Patch 6.28 ( Square Enix on Steam , 1 November 2022); its June 2024 post calls Dynamis’s Worlds the newly added ones. It takes you to another logical data centre for a while. Square Enix announced it in January 2022 and brought it in with Patch 6.18 on 5 July 2022, for travel between logical data centres within your own physical data centre ( Square Enix on Steam , 23 June 2022). Since Patch 7.0, players in Japan, North America and Europe can also travel across regions to the Oceanian data centre ( Square Enix on Steam , 19 June 2024). You start it with Visit Another Data Center on the character selection screen. While travelling, Square Enix says you can still progress the main story, find parties and use the Duty Finder. Matching itself is changing: Patch 7.57 brought same-region matchmaking to the Japanese data centres ( Square Enix on Steam , 13 October 2026), and Square Enix’s July release said North America and Europe would follow, without dates ( Square Enix’s release on ANN , 27 July 2026). Square Enix’s Lodestone post of 2 November now dates it: Patch 7.58, due on Tuesday 10 November 2026. See the Duty Finder . items.headline: Kings of Leon and Skepta lead a very heavy New Music Friday
items.summary: O My Beloved is the band’s tenth LP and a seventh UK No. 1 bid, The Fork and Knife is Skepta’s first solo album in seven years, and Royal Blood, Shygirl and Rex Orange County all land today.
items.matters: the Q4 release crunch is compressed into one Friday, and most of it will be invisible by January.
items.body: If you want to find out when our Official Charts Christmas Number 1 single for 2026 will be announced, you can find all the information HERE . With that in mind, let's check out what other albums and singles we have on offer for you this week. Kings of Leon begin their bid for a seventh Number 1 album with O My Beloved. This is the Tennessee veteran rockers' tenth LP overall and has been described as one of their most vulnerable projects to date, tackling extremely heavy subject matter. The band revisited the record during its creation, a process that inspired this change. If successful, they will join level with the likes of Pink Floyd , Blur , Prodigy and more for the most Number 1 albums in the UK. With four Number 1 albums in a row, British duo Royal Blood will look for their fifth on Dead Company. Adopting a raw and visceral sound, prepare for some knockout tunes and an album which runs at a blistering pace. The Spice Girls mark their 30th anniversary with compilation album, The Singles Collection. The collection is available in many different variants as a boxset, vinyl and CD . Marking three decades since Victoria Beckham , Geri Horner , Melanie C , Emma Bunton and Melanie B unleashed debut album Spice on the world, The Singles Collection comes almost 30 years to the week since the record that started it all landed. James Blunt is catching flights not feelings on comeback record, Airplane Mode. The follow up to 2023's Who We Used To Be , the Celebrity Traitors' finalist will be hoping to see the LP chart strongly and earn him a ninth Top 10 in a row. Recruiting a star-studded team containing the likes of Turnstile 's Brendan Yates, Dev Hynes ( Blood Orange ), Daniel Caesar , Mustafa and dexter in the newsagent, Rex Orange County has abandoned his wholly solo methods of work to unleash Dream Fatigue. The record follows a protagonist who tries on personas to win over a girl he loves. In an effort to be more than he is, he puts on all these characterisations, represented by the record's playful song titles such as 'Hannah Montana' and 'Elvis'. The Faith Tour from George Michael , a collection of previously unreleased recordings from his 1988 Paris concerts, is set to drop on multiple formats. This was the superstar's first solo concert tour, and is nod to his extraordinary talent as a performer and beyond. The Godfather of UK rap Skepta returns with The Fork and Knife, his first solo LP in seven years. Blending grime, garage, house, jungle, and electronic, Skepta explores what it means to British, his Nigerian heritage, and to exist between…

items.headline: Being Heumann reaches cinemas today
items.summary: Siân Heder’s follow-up to CODA stars Ruth Madeley as Judy Heumann and Mark Ruffalo, and covers the 1977 Section 504 sit-ins; Apple TV gets it on 13 November.
items.matters: it is an awards-season opener that arrives in theatres first, which is now the exception.
items.body: Apple Original Films unveiled the trailer for the critically acclaimed feature “Being Heumann.” Today, Apple Original Films unveiled the trailer for the critically acclaimed feature “Being Heumann,” the powerful new drama from writer, director and producer Siân Heder, which follows disability rights activist Judy Heumann, who leads more than a hundred young people in a radical act of defiance as they take over the San Francisco Federal building in a fight for equal rights. The trailer debuts just ahead of the Gala presentation of “Being Heumann” at the BFI London Film Festival, and following the film’s opening night premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival. “Being Heumann” will debut in select theaters on Friday, November 6, 2026 and premiere globally on Apple TV Friday, November 13, 2026. They wouldn’t take Judy Heumann’s phone calls, so she took their building. In 1977, a young disabled woman (Ruth Madeley) and a scrappy coalition of outsiders decide they’ve had enough. What begins as one impulsive act becomes the longest occupation of a federal building in American history, as hundreds spontaneously seize government offices and refuse to leave until the bureaucrat in their way (Mark Ruffalo) takes action. Bringing rebellion in all its forms to the hallowed halls, a movement’s accidental leaders struggle to find their path forward where none has ever been paved for them. Directed by Academy Award winner Heder (“CODA”) and based on true events, “Being Heumann” is the revolutionary, irreverent and deeply human story of the least likely people trying to pull off the impossible and change the lives of millions . “Being Heumann” is written, directed and produced by Heder, and co-written with Rebekah Taussig. The film is also produced by David Permut for Permut Presentations, John Beach, Kevin Cleary and Kevin Walsh for the Walsh Company. The film is executive produced by Jim LeBrecht, Diana Pokorny, Ann Molin and Kristen Joiner, co-author of Judy Heumann’s bestselling memoir, “Being Heumann: An Unrepentant Memoir of a Disability Rights Activist.” Dylan O’Brien, Madeline Delp, Roberta Colindrez, Jon Beavers, Antwan Tolliver, Ray Fisher, Andrew Pilkington, Michael Patrick Thornton, Russell Harvard, Daniel Durant, Charlie Rush-Reese, Rio Finnegan, D’Arcee Charington Neal, Will Brill, Rob Delaney, Matthew August Jeffers, Siena Rafter and Rein Barcel also star in the film. items.headline: Paul Greengrass and Andrew Garfield retell the Peasants’ Revolt
items.summary: The Uprising streams on Peacock today, with Garfield as a farmer leading the 1381 rising.
items.matters: the AP called it anachronistic enough to undercut its own argument, so treat it as a mood piece.
items.body: Don't be overwhelmed or waste an hour scrolling through your services to determine what to watch. We've got your back, whatever your mood. Mashable offers watch guides for all of the above, broken down by genre: comedy , thriller , horror , documentary , and animation , among others. But if you're seeking something brand new (or just new to streaming), we've got you covered there, too. In 2005, the missing persons case of Natalee Holloway became national news when the 18-year-old from Tennessee vanished in Aruba. She was last seen with Dutchman Joran van der Sloot, who was an early person of interest and over the years has told conflicting stories of what came next. I'm sorry, but isn't The 12 Dates of Christmas already a movie? The cheeseball 2011 Groundhog Day scenario starring Amy Smart as a Scroogey woman stuck in a time loop of dates to teach her a lesson about being nicer to people? Well, this isn't that. Hulu's identically named film reunites Pretty Little Liars stars Lucy Hale and Ian Harding in another romantic scenario, this time much less problematic than that show's student-teacher relationship. Will I be settling in to see Hale's character determined to thwart her own singlehood by going on 12 dates in 12 days at the busiest time of the year? As sure as a partridge in a pear tree. — S.C. Almost anything can be scary in the right circumstances. That, at least, seems to be what writer/director Yûta Shimotsu is going for in New Group , a horror comedy largely centered around human pyramids. These start to pop at Ai's (Anna Yamada) new high school, and it soon becomes clear that the phenomenon is more disturbing than simple gymnastics. — S.H. Andrew Garfield says "no kings" in The Uprising , the latest from director Paul Greengrass ( The Bourne Supremacy ). The film tells the story of England's 1381 Peasants' Revolt, with Garfield playing a fictionalized farmer at the center of it all. While The Uprising 's tale of standing up to tyranny is timely, critics found the film's execution lacking. As Mashable Entertainment Editor Kristy Puchko wrote in her review , "Greengrass gives us a bland, muddy slog with a black-and-white hero and villain, and an ending that is sure to satisfy no one." * — B.E. Romantic drama Charlie Harper hits digital this week — and no, it is not about someone named Charlie Harper, but rather about the love story between Charlie (Nick Robinson) and Harper (Emilia Jones). The film uses a nonlinear approach to tell the story of this pair's relationship, from their sweetest moments to their most tumultuous. Critics didn't fall…

items.body: Starting today, fans can explore even more KPop Demon Hunters on Netflix – all in one place. Introducing KPop Demon Hunters: For the Fans! , a first-of-its-kind, all-new destination on Netflix bringing together the ultimate collection of KPop Demon Hunters content that celebrates the music and characters fans love while discovering original and playful creations. Alongside the award-winning film, fan-favorite sing-along version and bonus content, some of the new content in the collection includes: all-new official choreography videos featuring new HUNTR/X animation and popular dance creators, and custom stop-motion animation videos showcasing HUNTR/X in a new style. HUNTR/X Backstage Pass: In this visually kinetic and fun stop-motion narrative 6-episode series, fans get exclusive access to HUNTR/X behind the scenes: rehearsals, photoshoots, costume fittings, and more. KPop Toy Creations: A 3-episode series of hand-made mini episodes inspired by KPop Demon Hunters and produced by one young filmmaking visionary, all between homework and dinner time. Play Games With Us: A 4-episode stop-motion animation series that's full of colorful competitions, challenges and fun, inspired by iconic scenes in KPop Demon Hunters . Fans can now dance like HUNTR/X and Saja Boys with a slate of official choreography content that turns the film’s biggest musical moments into something fans can learn and perform. Choose your bias. Three Hunters. Three signature styles. Choreographers Nain and Leejung Lee break down how Rumi, Mira, and Zoey’s personalities shape the way they move. KPop Demon Hunters , directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, became a global phenomenon shortly following its release on June 20, 2025. The film is Netflix's most popular film of all time, surpassing over 670 million views with 63 consecutive weeks on Netflix's Global Top 10. It swept every award category: winning Best Animated Feature at the Academy Awards, Critics' Choice Awards, Golden Globes, as well as ten Annie Awards. Its breakout song "Golden" became the first K-pop track to win both an Oscar and a Grammy. The soundtrack continues to make history as the first to place four songs simultaneously in the Billboard Hot 100 top ten, accumulating over 15 billion global streams. "Golden" held No. 1 on the Hot 100 for eight weeks — the longest such run by a female group this century — and was certified 5x…

items.body: Launched on 4 November, the European Chip Design Platform will mobilise €525 million in investment to stimulate a new generation of European chip design companies. ©putilov_denis Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, Henna Virkkunen launched the project, a key initiative under the EU Chips Act . Chip design is a core stage of the semiconductor value chain, where much of the industry's innovation emerges. European chip design companies currently account for less than 1% of global revenues in this segment. New manufacturing capacity in Europe will only be sustainable if there is enough demand for it, and much of that demand has to come from European designers. The European Chip Design Platform will give chip design companies access to chip design tools, design support services, intellectual property blocks, as well as access to manufacturing capacity on the platform. These resources are often the most expensive and the hardest to access for early-stage companies. The European Design Platform gives our chips start-ups and SMEs the support they need to overcome the barriers to turn their innovative ideas into silicon. It shows how Europe is ready to act on its technological sovereignty goals, not only through policy and promises, but also by investing in our…

items.headline: An AI toolbox for public administrations goes live
items.summary: the Commission published practical guidance and reusable examples on the Interoperable Europe portal to help agencies buy and deploy AI under the Apply AI Strategy.
items.matters: public-sector tenders will start citing it, and it reads as a template for what a compliant system looks like.
items.body: As a signed-in user you can create content, become a member of a community, receive notifications on your favourite solutions and topics, and access all other features available on the platform. Public administrations looking to adopt artificial intelligence can find practical tools, guidance and examples in the AI toolbox for the European public sector , available on the Interoperable Europe portal. The toolbox supports the implementation of the European Commission’s Apply AI Strategy by helping administrations identify resources they can use and adapt to their needs. The Apply AI Strategy sets out actions to accelerate AI adoption across Europe’s key industries and the public sector, strengthening competitiveness and technological sovereignty. It includes a commitment to build a shared repository of practical, open-source and reusable tools and solutions to support AI interoperability in public administrations. Developed as part of Interoperable Europe, the toolbox contributes to delivering this commitment. It brings together resources that address the organisational, technical and skills challenges administrations face when introducing AI into public services. AI standards and tools: resources supporting interoperability, reusable open source solutions and tools for assessing AI systems. Use cases: examples from European public administrations, covering internal processes, public service delivery and policymaking. Skills and training opportunities: courses, webinars and learning materials to help public officials build their understanding of AI. Legal and procurement guidance: information on the regulatory framework and resources to support the procurement of AI solutions. For example, the tools section links to OpenForm, an AI-assisted application tool that provides conversational support for completing forms, uploading documents, and generating PDFs. Administrations exploring how AI could help users navigate application procedures can use OpenForm as a starting point to assess whether an existing solution could meet their needs. The toolbox also helps administrations learn from one another. Its use-case section features F13, a generative AI text assistant introduced by Baden-Württemberg’s public administration innovation lab. Its functions include summarising documents, supporting research and generating text, illustrating how AI can assist with everyday administrative work. The toolbox is part of the Portal’s wider AI in the public sector space , which brings together related news, guidance, tools, use cases and events. Other resources, including…

items.headline: Vermont has spent nearly a billion dollars on Lake Champlain and the green slime keeps coming back
items.summary: ProPublica and Seven Days went through the monitoring data and found seven of fifteen sampling stations over the phosphorus limit every year since 2015, a state audit that was never done, and two agencies splitting farm enforcement between them.
items.body: On the last day of August, Jeff van den Noort spotted thick swirls of neon green film coating the water just steps from his home in Vermont. He waded in up to his ankles and dipped a jar to get a sample of the scum. It wasn’t the first time he’d seen the slime. Since his parents bought the house on an island in Lake Champlain in 1966, van den Noort has spent part of nearly every summer in this quiet spot. Back then, the lake was clear. But he began to witness the water’s deterioration as he grew older, especially after he moved into the home full time in 2010 to care for his ailing mother. That day in late August was the worst he’d seen all summer. Later that week, van den Noort grabbed a bucket, a few Mason jars and a smartphone and got into his rusty Saab. He drove past the boat launches, frozen-in-time general stores and windswept pastures of the lake’s islands in northern Vermont and stopped at four other spots along the shore. Each time, he collected some murky water, gauged how thick the muck was, took a few photos and jotted down the weather conditions. He then uploaded his report to an online database. Van den Noort was one part of a large volunteer effort to monitor a problem that has plagued Lake Champlain, which supplies drinking water to about 200,000 people. In recent decades, blooms of potentially toxic cyanobacteria, often called blue-green algae, have killed pets, forced beaches to close and hurt business and property values along the shores of this iconic Vermont feature. Just over a decade ago, state leaders seemed to be doing just that. In 2015, then-Gov. Peter Shumlin stood a few feet from Lake Champlain by the Burlington waterfront and signed Vermont’s Clean Water Act. It promised to tighten limits on pollution and provide funding to clean up the state’s waterways. The move was a response to ratcheting pressure from environmentalists and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. The EPA had been telling Vermont officials for years that they needed to take much stronger action. In 2016, the agency finalized tougher cleanup targets that the state must meet by 2036. But after 10 years and nearly a billion dollars spent on water quality projects and programs, Vermont’s cleanup effort is faltering. In a little-noticed letter to the head of Vermont’s Department of Environmental Conservation last year, the EPA’s regional administrator warned that the state was “not on track” to meet its cleanup goal and would need to more than double its annual pace. Halfway through the two-decade timetable, Vermont has achieved only 35% of the goal,…
